title: Patterns
examples: Teacher, how do I find the next shape?
Can we make a pattern with toys?
What is the rule for this colour pattern?

explain.say: Look at these shapes. We see a circle, then a square. Say circle, then square.
We can make a pattern by repeating these shapes. Circle, square, circle, square. This is a repeating pattern.
Sometimes we repeat colours. Look at red, blue, red, blue. The colours go back to the start.
If we see green, yellow, green, yellow. We know the next colour must be green again.
This pattern is easy to see. It goes circle, square, circle, square. What comes next after the last square?
In real life, patterns help us know what to expect. Think about the days of the week. Monday comes after Sunday.

faq.q: How do I know which colour comes next?
faq.a: You look at the pattern before it. If it was red then blue, it will probably be red again.
asks: Can you tell me the next colour?

faq.q: Do patterns always repeat the same thing?
faq.a: Most simple patterns repeat the same group of items over and over again. This is how we find what comes next.
asks: Is it always the same order?
Does it have to be the same shape?

faq.q: What if the pattern is tricky?
faq.a: If it is tricky, look very closely at the first few items. The pattern rule is always hidden in the beginning.
asks: How do I solve a hard pattern?

faq.q: Can I use numbers in patterns?
faq.a: Yes, numbers make patterns too. For example, counting up by two: two, four, six, eight.

faq.q: Do shapes have to be perfect?
faq.a: For simple patterns, we use clear shapes like circles and squares. You can use any shape you like to make a pattern.
asks: Do the shapes have to be neat?

facts: Patterns are things that repeat in a predictable way.
You can find patterns in nature, like the rings of a tree.
Patterns can use colours, shapes, or numbers.
To find what comes next, you must find the pattern rule first.

quiz.say: What comes next in the pattern: Red, Blue, Red, Blue?
quiz.why: The pattern repeats the pair Red and Blue, so the next colour must be Red.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might think the whole pair repeats at once.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it is the colour that follows Red in the pair.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might think the colours are changing suddenly.

quiz.say: What comes next in the pattern: Circle, Square, Circle, Square?
quiz.why: The pattern repeats the pair Circle then Square, so the next shape must be a Circle.

wrong.0: This is tempting because the last shape was a Square, so you might repeat it.
wrong.1: This is tempting because you might think the whole pair restarts.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you might try a new shape that doesn't fit the rule.

quiz.say: If the pattern is Yellow, Green, Yellow, Green, what is the next colour?
quiz.why: The pattern repeats Yellow then Green, so the next colour must be Yellow.

wrong.0: This is tempting because you might think the pattern restarts with both colours.
wrong.2: This is tempting because Green is the colour that follows Yellow in the pair.
wrong.3: This is tempting because you might guess a completely new colour.
